verified: Voyager project scientist Linda Spilker told Space.com that Voyager 1 is about 16.1 billion miles away and is the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth; the 24-hour one-way light travel time follows directly from that distance, and the mission team communicates via NASA's Deep Space Network.
unconfirmed: Space.com does not cite a NASA press release or independent measurement, and the exact timestamp of 5:16 a.m. EST is a computed marker rather than an instrument reading; the article also rounds the distance differently in two places ("about 16 billion miles" and "about 16.1 billion miles").

verified: 旅行者1号于 1977 年 9 月 5 日发射、2012 年 8 月 25 日成为首个进入星际空间的人造物体、旅行者2号于 2018 年 11 月跟进，这些均为公开的任务记录；项目科学家 Linda Spilker 向 Space.com 确认了“地球与旅行者相距正好 24 光时”这一时刻及约 161 亿英里的距离。
unconfirmed: 1 光日的精确达成时刻与对应距离来自任务团队的计算，由 Space.com 单篇报道呈现，文中未引用 NASA 官方公告或独立测量；报道也未说明在电力与仪器持续衰减的情况下，探测器还能维持通信与科学观测多久。

titles.en: Voyager 1 becomes first spacecraft to reach one light-day from Earth
titles.zh: 旅行者1号距地球满1光日，成首个抵达的人造物体
